title: Dark Factory
pitch: A standalone world-building editor: author maps from an asset library, save what a game can load.

title: Gooey
pitch: Game and tool interfaces for Bevy 0.20: a skin, ready-made widgets and keyboard and gamepad navigation, built on Bevy's own headless widgets (the behaviour with no look of its own).

title: Elements
pitch: Living environments for Bevy 0.20: a sun and moon on real ephemerides, the bright-star sky, a seeded climate that schedules hourly weather, a GPU wind field, volumetric clouds, rain and snow, lightning and thunder, fog, heightfield terrain with erosion and flooding, ground cover, rocks, dust, paths and trails — all in compute shaders, for anyone building an open world that has to look alive without a weather artist.

title: Flora
pitch: **Parametric, stylized procedural trees for Bevy that grow over time**, for anyone building a forest without modelling one: pick one of 20 presets or tune every parameter, spawn a component, and watch a seedling grow into a mature tree. The same seed always gives the same tree.

title: Isomesh
pitch: Signed distance field in, triangles out: isosurface extraction for Rust voxel games and CAD tools, with a Bevy plugin.

title: Lights
pitch: Practical lights for Bevy: the fires a scene's props actually carry — a budgeted pool of real lights over thousands of virtual ones, with shader flames and the flicker that makes them read.

title: Light Grid
pitch: An illuminance grid that creature AI can read: "how bright is it here, and which way is brighter", computed on the CPU per cell, for games where things flee or seek the light.

title: Society
pitch: Give your Bevy world a living society: villagers who remember, gossip, take sides, fall out and make up, and whose days you can script.

title: Stigmergy
pitch: Fading marks on a grid that a crowd coordinates through, like ant trails: for game AI that should converge, scatter or rally without any agent planning a route.

title: Orca
pitch: Walkers that steer around each other without colliding: ORCA (optimal reciprocal collision avoidance) as a plain library on `bevy_math`'s `Vec2`, for crowds in games.

title: Speech Bubbles
pitch: Speech balloons, barks, conversation graphs and a skinnable dialog box for Bevy games whose characters talk.

title: Carnage
pitch: Wounds that peel to the bone, bleed, pool and dry, and bodies that break into chunks, for Bevy characters, deterministic to the bit.

title: Fairy
pitch: Let a coding agent look inside a running Bevy game, drive it, and ask the person playing it for help — without touching your desktop.

title: Siren
pitch: Sound for Bevy 0.20 that decides *what* plays and *how loud*: cues with variants, buses that duck, a voice budget that refuses politely, music that changes on the bar, and a log of what played and why.

title: Devshot
pitch: A frame on demand: touch a sentinel file and the next frame writes a PNG, straight from the GPU.

title: Presence
pitch: Presence for Bevy: the crates a VR game needs to put a player in a room with a character who listens, answers, looks at them and moves its mouth.
